scope: Basic finite-length cancellation and regular-scalar cokernel formula without adding finite-length assumptions to the formal regularity identity.
Exact-sequence Euler additivity and middle finite scalar homology from finiteness at the two outer terms; linear-equivalence transport.
Over a Noetherian ring, finite modules and support containment transfer finite scalar homology from finite scalar cokernel of the ambient module; actual submodule and subquotient corollaries.

Native RelSeries bottom-to-top prime filtration Euler sum plus minimal-label occurrence counts equal native localized lengths, using the same filtration. Generic statements require supplied filtration, not Noetherianity; existence is deduced for finite modules over Noetherian rings.
For a finite module over a Noetherian local ring, support dimension at most one and finite scalar cokernel imply the Euler-weighted associativity sum over minimal support points.

The usual endpoint derives the dimension bound from scalar membership in the maximal ideal and finite scalar cokernel. Scalar regularity on the original module additionally gives the pure cokernel-length associativity formula.

assumptions: Module.length A (M / range(lsmul A M t)) is not infinity
associativity.formula: principalEuler(M,t) = finsum over q minimal in support_A(M) of length_{A_q}(LocalizedModule(q.primeCompl,M)).toNat * principalEuler(A/q,t), with natural lengths cast to integers.
associativity.regular_endpoint: Module.principalCokernel_associativity adds IsSMulRegular M t and replaces both Euler integers with principal-cokernel lengths.
associativity.zero_dimensional_case: Native 02QF sums over nonclosed support points. Under dimension at most one these are minimal, but the closed point can be minimal in dimension zero. The proof first replaces order by Euler only at nonclosed points, then extends the sum with the zero Euler contribution at the closed point. It does not extend the raw order sum or invoke the dimension-exactly-one equality of index sets.
associativity.regression: For a field and zero scalar, principalEuler is zero while Ring.ord of zero is one; test covers this distinction.
